faqs.question: What size air filter do I need?
faqs.answer: You need the exact Width × Length × Depth printed on your current filter or measured from the filter slot. Enter those three numbers in our size finder to shop the matching HVAC filter.

faqs.question: How do I measure an air filter?
faqs.answer: Measure Width (side to side), Length (top to bottom), and Depth (thickness) in inches. Use the nominal size on the frame label when present; otherwise measure the filter itself and round to the nearest standard size.

faqs.question: What is the difference between nominal and actual filter size?
faqs.answer: Nominal size is the labeled size (for example 20×25×1). Actual size is slightly smaller so the filter slides into the slot. Filter Hero lists both on each size page so you can verify fit.

faqs.question: How often should I change my HVAC filter?
faqs.answer: Most homes should change filters every 30 to 90 days. Pets, allergies, dust, and a fan that runs constantly pull you toward 30. Use Filter Clock: tell us about the house and we'll give you the date — then buy the pack that matches a year of air.

faqs.question: What MERV rating should I buy?
faqs.answer: MERV 8 is standard everyday filtration. MERV 11 is better for pets and mild allergies. MERV 13 offers higher filtration for asthma and sensitivities. MERV 8 Carbon adds odor reduction. Confirm your HVAC system supports higher MERV before upgrading.

faqs.question: Do you sell filters for Carrier, Trane, Honeywell, and other HVAC brands?
faqs.answer: Yes. Filter Hero replacement filters are made to the same Width × Length × Depth as OEM media for major HVAC brands. Shop by brand, model number, or OEM part number, then choose MERV 8, MERV 8 Carbon, 11, or 13. Sizes we do not list can be quoted.
